dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second projection from a LocalDef004 object: a function sending a vertex and graph to a natural number.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first projection from a LocalDef004 object: a measure on simple graphs with vertex type Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Extracts the graphLaw measure used by the integral, which for LocalDef001 is the binomial random-graph measure.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: An n- and p-indexed structure whose constructor stores a measure on simple graphs on Fin n and a natural-valued vertex-degree observable.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n and p, constructs the model with graphLaw = SimpleGraph.binomialRandom (Fin n) p and degree(v,G) = G.degree v.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Identifies the integral exactly as the expected ordinary degree of v in a binomial random simple graph on n labeled vertices with edge parameter p.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite vertex type Fin n, the subtype of neighbors of any vertex in any simple graph is finite.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq

dependency_coverage.name: Fin

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub

dependency_coverage.name: InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.integral

dependency_coverage.name: Membership.mem

dependency_coverage.name: Nat

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instRCLike

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
p is an arbitrary real number bundled with a proof that 0 <= p <= 1.
v is an arbitrary vertex of Fin n, the n-element labeled vertex set.
hypotheses: There are no additional explicit hypotheses beyond the binder types; in particular, the unit-interval condition on p is carried by its subtype and the existence of v entails that Fin n is inhabited for that instance of the assertion.
conclusions: The integral of the real-cast degree of v over the binomial random simple-graph measure on Fin n with edge parameter p is exactly ((n - 1) cast to Real) * p.
Equivalently, the expected degree of every fixed vertex in this random graph equals (n - 1)p.
mathematical_definitions: The random graph law is SimpleGraph.binomialRandom(Fin n, p), obtained from a Bernoulli random set of non-loop unordered vertex pairs.
For a sampled graph G, degree(v,G) is G.degree v, the natural-number cardinality of the neighbor set of v.
The integrand casts this natural degree to a real number before integration.
The right side first computes natural subtraction n - 1, casts it to the reals, and multiplies by the underlying real value of p.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every n, every edge parameter p in the closed interval [0,1], and every vertex v among n labeled vertices, the expected degree of v in the binomial random simple graph with parameter p is exactly (n - 1)p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The graphs are simple graphs: loops and multiple edges are absent, so a vertex has at most n - 1 possible neighbors.
The vertex set is specifically Fin n, and the identity concerns a single arbitrary fixed vertex rather than a random vertex or an average over vertices.
The edge parameter includes both endpoints p = 0 and p = 1.
Natural subtraction is used on the right: n - 1 is truncated at zero before being cast to the reals.
When n = 0 there is no term v : Fin 0, so the universally quantified assertion has no vertex instance and is vacuous for that n.
When n = 1, the only vertex has degree zero and the right side is (1 - 1)p = 0.
The statement is an exact expectation identity only; it asserts no variance, concentration, independence theorem in its conclusion, or asymptotic behavior.
